title: Where did the distilled image information go? Diagnostics for the Experiment 2 student

experiment2.note: the full run whose output is attached; its student, head, teacher, observations and evaluation are reused

decision_rules.A: Present but not linearly readable from f(p) is supported if A2 (h(f(p))) or A3 ([f(p), h(f(p))]) beats A1 (f(p)) in top-1 mIoU with a 95 % paired-bootstrap interval that excludes 0; otherwise it is not supported.
decision_rules.B: Generalization gap = mean train cosine − mean val cosine (bootstrap over scenes), for the student (B1) and for the head-only baseline on frozen Sonata (B2). A student gap much larger than B2's (the interval of the difference of gaps above 0) indicates that continued training fitted the 200 train scenes.
decision_rules.C: With one training seed per student and 50 val scenes, differences under about 1 mIoU are not resolvable. If |student_attn − student_mean| < 1 mIoU or its 95 % interval includes 0, report "no evidence that learned attention matters"; never claim equivalence. Otherwise report the direction and size.

check_rules.A_reproduction: Experiment 2's saved probes (T#0-2) applied to f(p) recomputed now on every val scene give A1'. The check passes if every val scene was encoded with the same number of tiles as in Experiment 2 and |A1' - A1| is no larger than A1's standard deviation over probe seeds, at top-1 and at top-3. Identical counts are not required: the smoke run of 2026-11-12 found counts up to 58 apart on one scene, most likely because the sparse-convolution kernels are chosen by timing in each session (two passes in one session are bit-identical). User decision, 2026-11-12.
